title: San Antonio Cooling
desc: Need help keeping the moisture in your home under control? Rosenberg Indoor Comfort has the specialists to help you lower your humidity levels.

blocks.text: Controlling the humidity levels in your home can be an extremely important thing, although many people often over look how much moisture is floating around in their homes.

The reason why it is so important is the fact that moisture in the air can lead to a ton of nasty things, such as mildew and mold, which can form in and around the insides of your walls, at the base of your floorboards, on your ceilings and many other places.
If not removed quickly, mold can cause all sorts of damage to your home, which can ultimately cost a massive amount of money to have removed.

The worst part is, if mold does end up developing in your home, you do not really have a choice to remove it or not, due to the fact that mold can cause huge health problems to people in the house, who are probably inhaling the mold without knowing it each and every day. Here are three of the top things you can do to normalize the humidity in your home.

Mold and mildew is not going to develop overnight, and there are some signs that you should watch out for, which are indicative that you have a developing mold problem. If there is condensation on the inside of your windows, or you start to notice mildew developing anywhere on your walls, this is a very bad sign and you should have your home inspected as soon as possible.

A great option to regulate the humidity level in your home is to simply go out and purchase a humidifier, which can effectively normalize the humidity levels in your home. You may want to go out and buy one of the products that tests the humidity levels in your home as well, but you really should only purchase a humidifier after you have had a professional company check your house out and advise you on what to do.

Without a doubt, the best thing to do if you think you are having problems with the humidity in your home is to call someone who knows what they are doing. They can check the humidity levels out in your home and will do a detailed inspection to determine if you have any developing mold or mildew problems, and the best course of acting to have the problem rectified.
